title: Synthetic service CRUD professional test design
limitations: Design-only pilot: no target, credential, database, or deployed contract was supplied; every case remains not_run.

access_control_matrix.expected: Authorized soft delete with audit event

test_cases.title: Collection returns bounded public fields
test_cases.scenario: Request the first collection page with default filters
preconditions: Synthetic viewer is authorized to read services
steps: Send GET /services?page=1&per_page=10 using an opaque viewer credential reference
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 200 returns at most 10 documented records, external UUIDs, pagination metadata, and no internal numeric identifiers.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response and query correlation ID

test_cases.title: Invalid pagination is rejected safely
test_cases.scenario: Request a page size above the documented maximum
preconditions: Synthetic viewer is authorized to read services
steps: Send GET /services?page=1&per_page=1001
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented validation status and error code without returning an unbounded collection.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Bounds protect data and service capacity.

test_cases.title: Authorized UUID returns service detail
test_cases.scenario: Request an existing authorized service UUID
preconditions: Synthetic service UUID belongs to the viewer scope
steps: Send GET /services/{uuid} for the synthetic authorized UUID
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 200 returns the matching external UUID and documented public fields without internal identifiers.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Detail contract is a core read path.

test_cases.title: Cross-owner UUID is denied
test_cases.scenario: Request another owner scope service UUID
preconditions: Two isolated synthetic owner scopes exist
steps: Authenticate with owner A credential reference
Send GET for owner B synthetic service UUID
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the approved forbidden or non-enumerating not-found response and discloses no owner B fields.

test_cases.title: Valid create persists one auditable record
test_cases.scenario: Create one service with valid synthetic input
preconditions: Synthetic administrator and unique fixture key exist
steps: Send POST /services with the approved synthetic payload
Read the created record and audit event using the returned UUID
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 201 returns an external UUID, persists exactly one record, and writes one correlated create audit event.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response, persistence query, audit correlation ID
cleanup: Delete or deactivate the synthetic created record through approved cleanup

test_cases.title: Duplicate create rolls back
test_cases.scenario: Submit a duplicate unique service key
preconditions: One synthetic service already owns the fixture unique key
steps: Send POST /services with the existing synthetic unique key
Count records and related rows for the key
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented duplicate error and creates no service, relation, or audit success record.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Duplicate and partial writes corrupt integrity.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response and before/after row counts

test_cases.title: PUT replaces complete resource
test_cases.scenario: Replace an existing resource with complete valid input
steps: Send PUT /services/{uuid} with every required field
Read the resource and audit event
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 200 returns the documented replacement, persists it exactly once, and records one update audit event.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response, before/after snapshot, audit event

test_cases.title: PUT missing required field preserves resource
test_cases.scenario: Replace a resource while omitting a required field
steps: Send PUT /services/{uuid} without the required name
Read the resource after rejection
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented validation error and every persisted field remains equal to the pre-test snapshot.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Invalid replacement must not erase fields.

test_cases.title: PATCH updates only allowlisted field
test_cases.scenario: Patch one allowlisted field with the current version
preconditions: Synthetic service snapshot and version exist
steps: Send PATCH /services/{uuid} changing only name with the current version
Compare every persisted field with the snapshot
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 200 changes only name, increments the documented version, preserves unrelated fields, and writes one audit event.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response and field-by-field before/after snapshot

test_cases.title: PATCH stale version rejects lost update
test_cases.scenario: Patch a service using a stale version
preconditions: Synthetic service version advanced after the client snapshot
steps: Send PATCH /services/{uuid} with the stale version
Read the current resource and audit events
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented conflict response and preserves the current record without a successful update audit event.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized conflict response, current record, audit query

test_cases.title: Administrator soft-deletes service
test_cases.scenario: Soft-delete an active synthetic service as administrator
preconditions: Synthetic deletable service has no blocking dependency
steps: Send DELETE /services/{uuid} as synthetic administrator
Read the service through normal and privileged queries
Read its audit event
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented success, normal reads no longer expose the service, privileged state shows soft-deleted status, and one delete audit event exists.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Deletion changes availability and retention state.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response, normal/privileged reads, audit event
cleanup: Restore the synthetic service through approved fixture reset

test_cases.title: Viewer cannot delete service
test_cases.scenario: Attempt to delete an active service as viewer
preconditions: Synthetic viewer and active service exist
steps: Capture the service snapshot
Send DELETE /services/{uuid} as synthetic viewer
Read the service and audit events
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 403 is returned, the service snapshot is unchanged, no delete audit success exists, and no internal authorization detail is exposed.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Broken function-level authorization can destroy data.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response, before/after snapshot, audit query

test_cases.title: Repeated delete follows idempotency contract
test_cases.scenario: Repeat delete for an already soft-deleted synthetic service
preconditions: Synthetic service is already soft-deleted by an authorized prior step
steps: Send DELETE /services/{uuid} again as synthetic administrator
Count delete audit events and verify final state
test_cases.expected_result: The API returns the documented repeat-delete response, final state remains soft-deleted, and no duplicate destructive side effect occurs.
test_cases.priority_rationale: Retries must not multiply side effects.
evidence_requirements: Sanitized response, final state, audit count
cleanup: Restore the synthetic service through approved fixture reset
